paper.title: Analytic reproducibility in articles receiving open data badges at the journal Psychological Science: an observational study

findings.evidence: 'percent reproducible with author involvement' is reported with different values. Abstract: 34 % | Table 1: 24 %. Agreeing reports: 1 location(s) [Abstract] vs 1 [Table 1].
findings.question_for_authors: Which value of 'percent reproducible with author involvement' is correct (34 % or 24 %)?

findings.evidence: Re-computed 'n decision errors reported in text' = 1 values does not match reported 3 values (Results p.4); relative difference 66.7%. Source: our re-run. No stored output from the authors was recorded for this value; it has not passed the reproduction gate, so it stays yellow. Check that the denominator, subset and filters match the paper's before asking the authors.
findings.question_for_authors: Which code version, data version, seed or settings produced the reported value?

findings.evidence: No dependency specification found (requirements.txt, environment.yml, renv.lock, ...).
findings.question_for_authors: Which software and library versions were used?

findings.evidence: Rmd outputs (deep_checks.py): timeSummary computed in chunk(s) unnamed but never printed or written; the knitted output (results/manuscript.pdf) can only hold what is printed: caption. The stored result for timeSummary is therefore not in the materials.
findings.question_for_authors: Can the timeSummary table be added to the stored output?

findings.evidence: Results: 'two decision errors ... and one decision error with the opposite pattern' (3 in total). The released data contain 1 row with comparisonOutcome == DECISION_ERROR (dataID 459, reported 0.09 vs obtained 0.02); decisionErrors_nonsig (reported < .05, obtained >= .05) = 0. The authors' stored manuscript.tex line 412-414 prints '2 decision errors ... and 1 decision error with the opposite pattern', so the text and the stored output agree with each other but not with the released data file.
findings.question_for_authors: Which rows in data_values.csv correspond to the two decision errors with a reported non-significant p-value?

findings.evidence: Sample: '789 discrete numerical values reported in 27 articles'. data_articles.csv has 25 rows (25 distinct articleIDs), and data_values.csv covers the same 25 articles; the paper elsewhere reports 25 articles throughout. The authors' stored manuscript.tex line 285 also prints 27, so the discrepancy is between the paper and its own data file, not a transcription slip.
findings.question_for_authors: Were target values taken from 25 or 27 articles? Which two articles would be missing from data_articles.csv?

findings.evidence: Claim 'Fewer than half of the 25 badge articles are not fully reproducible after author contact (i.e. at least 50% are fully reproducible)' holds in 50% of 16 universes. Single changes that flip it: denominator=reusable.
findings.question_for_authors: Was the result checked under denominator=reusable?
